rationale:
Split into five children. Each is a distinct mathematical step that the supplied proof already treats separately. With them, the parent becomes a ~25-line assembly.

**Children and the parent steps they cover**
(1) range_projection_diff (parent step 1, G0). B ↦ (range B).starProjection is differentiable at every injective B. The proof uses the Gram formula B(B*B)⁻¹B* on the open set where B*B is a unit. This reusable fact is strictly stronger than the continuity claim of the unrelated-branch node root.submanifold_tangent-a1.range_projection_continuous-a1, which cannot be depended on across branches.
(2) immersion_left_inverse (steps 2–3, G1). A C¹ map with injective Dψ(x₀) has a left inverse g, differentiable at ψ(x₀), with g∘ψ = id near x₀. The inverse function theorem is applied to L∘ψ (L a linear left inverse of Dψ(x₀)) instead of Ξ(x,q) = ψ(x)+q. The conclusion is the same, without the product space or the dimension count.
(3) tangent_projection_extension (steps 1, 3–5; depends on (1) and (2) and on SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter, Simon 4.2). On M near ψ(x₀), tangentProjection M agrees with Q := Πr∘Dψ∘g, which is differentiable at ψ(x₀), and Q(ψ x) = (range Dψ(x)).starProjection near x₀. It takes as hypothesis the chart instance (T) of (TH1), not the full (TH).
(4) projection_field_identity (step 8, G2). Differentiating Q(ψ x)(Dψ(x)b) = Dψ(x)b at x₀ gives DQ(ψx₀)(Dψ(x₀)a)(Dψ(x₀)b) = D²ψ(x₀)[a,b] − Q(ψx₀)D²ψ(x₀)[a,b]. This is the computational content of Simon 4.26 in frame-free form.
(5) fderiv_within_chart_direction (steps 6–7). M generally lacks unique differentiability, so fderivWithin on M agrees with an extension's derivative only on the tangent cone. Chart directions Dψ(x₀)a lie in that cone. This is the subtle point flagged by the parent audit.

**Assembly** (verified in Lean)
- Get (T) from (TH).1 n N 2 … (1 ≤ 2), then obtain Q from (3).
- The fixing hypothesis of (4) comes from (3)(iii) plus Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff and LinearMap.mem_range_self.
- Apply (5) with f := tangentProjection M and g := Q, then apply (4).
- Rewrite Q(ψ x₀) = tangentProjection M (ψ x₀) using Filter.EventuallyEq.eq_of_nhdsWithin at ψ(x₀) ∈ M.
- Unfold secondFundamentalForm and normalPart. Regularity facts come from ContDiffOn.contDiffAt and ContDiffAt.fderiv_right.

subproblems.title: Differentiability of the orthogonal projection onto the range of an injective linear map
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ and write ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d). Equip L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) := (ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝᴺ) and L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) := (ℝᴺ →L[ℝ] ℝᴺ) with the operator norm. For B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) let Πr(B) := (LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap).starProjection ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) be the orthogonal projection of ℝᴺ onto the range of B. If A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) is injective, then the map Πr : L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) → L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ), B ↦ Πr(B), is Fréchet differentiable at A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), Function.Injective A → DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun B : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N ↦ (LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap).starProjection) A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (parent G0) of the supplied proof of second_fundamental_form_chart_formula. There Π(A) = A(A*A)⁻¹A* is the orthogonal projection onto range A for injective A, and Π is smooth on the open set of injective maps. Only differentiability at an injective point is used, and that is what is proved here.
Notation: ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d); L(X, Y) := (X →L[ℝ] Y) with the operator norm; for a linear map B, range B := LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap and K.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of the ambient space onto the subspace K. For B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) let B* ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ) be its adjoint (⟨B*w, v⟩ = ⟨w, Bv⟩; Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint). Let G(B) := B* ∘ B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) be the Gram operator. Let Ring.inverse be inversion in the Banach algebra L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), whose multiplication is composition: it is the inverse on units and 0 elsewhere. Put F(B) := B ∘ (Ring.inverse(G(B)) ∘ B*) ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ). Fix an injective A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ).
1. (The adjoint is a continuous real-linear map.) The map adj : L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) → L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ), B ↦ B*, is additive and satisfies (cB)* = c B* for c ∈ ℝ, because complex conjugation is trivial on ℝ. It is an isometry (‖B*‖ = ‖B‖), hence continuous. So adj is a continuous ℝ-linear map and is differentiable everywhere, with derivative adj itself. [Lean: Mathlib's ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is only conjugate-linear (≃ₗᵢ⋆[ℝ]), so build the ℝ-CLM as ⟨{toFun := fun B ↦ ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint B, map_add' := by simp, map_smul' := by simp}, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint.continuous⟩.]
2. (G(A) is a unit.) If G(A)v = 0, then 0 = ⟨A*Av, v⟩ = ⟨Av, Av⟩ = ‖Av‖², so Av = 0 and v = 0 because A is injective. Thus G(A) is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, hence bijective. Its linear inverse is continuous because ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional. So G(A) has a two-sided inverse in L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), i.e. IsUnit (G(A)). [Lean: ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp_self_injective_iff gives injectivity, since ⇑(A† ∘L A) is definitionally ⇑A† ∘ ⇑A. Then LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv and (ContinuousLinearEquiv.unitsEquiv ℝ (Rn n)).symm produce the unit.]
3. (Invertibility persists near A.) The map B ↦ G(B) = adj(B) ∘ B is continuous: adj is continuous and composition of operators is continuous. The units of the complete normed ring L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) form an open set (Units.isOpen). Hence S := {B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) : G(B) is a unit} is open, contains A by step 2, and so is a neighbourhood of A.
4. (Explicit formula on S.) Let B ∈ S and H := Ring.inverse(G(B)). Then G(B) ∘ H = id (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel). Fix w ∈ ℝᴺ and put p := F(B)w = B(H(B*w)), so p ∈ range B. Let u ∈ range B, say u = Bv. Then ⟨w − p, Bv⟩ = ⟨B*(w − p), v⟩ = ⟨B*w − G(B)(H(B*w)), v⟩ = ⟨B*w − B*w, v⟩ = 0. So p ∈ range B and w − p ⊥ range B. By the characterisation of orthogonal projection (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero), Πr(B)w = p = F(B)w. As w is arbitrary, Πr(B) = F(B) for every B ∈ S.
5. (F is differentiable at A.) The identity B ↦ B is differentiable, and B ↦ B* is differentiable by step 1. Hence B ↦ G(B) = adj(B) ∘ B is differentiable at A, since a composition of operator-valued maps differentiable at A is differentiable at A (DifferentiableAt.clm_comp). Ring.inverse is differentiable at the unit G(A) (differentiableAt_inverse; its derivative is T ↦ −G(A)⁻¹ T G(A)⁻¹). By the chain rule, B ↦ Ring.inverse(G(B)) is differentiable at A. Two more applications of DifferentiableAt.clm_comp show that F(B) = B ∘ (Ring.inverse(G(B)) ∘ adj(B)) is differentiable at A.
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, Πr and F agree on the neighbourhood S of A, i.e. Πr =ᶠ[𝓝 A] F. A map that agrees near A with a map differentiable at A is differentiable at A (DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence B ↦ (LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap).starProjection is differentiable at A. ∎
proof_key_steps: B ↦ B* is a continuous real-linear map, hence differentiable.
A injective ⇒ the Gram operator A*A is injective, hence a unit of L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ).
Units form an open set, so S = {B : B*B is a unit} is a neighbourhood of A.
On S, (range B).starProjection = B (B*B)⁻¹ B*, by the orthogonality characterisation of the projection.
B ↦ B (B*B)⁻¹ B* is differentiable at A (clm_comp, and differentiability of Ring.inverse at units).
Agreement on a neighbourhood transfers differentiability to the range projection.

subproblems.title: Local left inverse of an immersion, differentiable at the image point (inverse function theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ and x₀ ∈ ℝⁿ, where ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). Assume ψ is C¹ at x₀ (ContDiffAt ℝ 1 ψ x₀, i.e. ψ is C¹ on some neighbourhood of x₀). Assume also that its derivative Dψ(x₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ is injective. Then there is a map g : ℝᴺ → ℝⁿ that is Fréchet differentiable at ψ(x₀) and satisfies g(ψ(x)) = x for every x in some neighbourhood of x₀.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (x₀ : Rn n), ContDiffAt ℝ 1 ψ x₀ → Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀) → ∃ g : Rn N → Rn n, DifferentiableAt ℝ g (ψ x₀) ∧ ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, g (ψ x) = x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 (parent G1) of the supplied proof of second_fundamental_form_chart_formula. Those steps produce a map π, differentiable at y₀ = ψ(x₀), with π(ψ(x)) = x on a neighbourhood V₀ of x₀; this is exactly the present conclusion. The parent obtains π from the inverse function theorem applied to Ξ(x, q) = ψ(x) + q on ℝⁿ × (range Dψ(x₀))^⊥. Here the same theorem is applied to the n-dimensional map L ∘ ψ, where L is a linear left inverse of Dψ(x₀). This gives the same conclusion without the product space or the dimension count.
Notation: A₀ := Dψ(x₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), y₀ := ψ(x₀).
1. (A continuous linear left inverse of A₀.) A₀ is injective, so its kernel is {0}. Hence there is a linear map L : ℝᴺ → ℝⁿ with L ∘ A₀ = id_{ℝⁿ}: the images under A₀ of a basis of ℝⁿ are linearly independent; extend them to a basis of ℝᴺ, and define L by L(A₀eᵢ) := eᵢ for a basis (eᵢ) of ℝⁿ and L := 0 on the added vectors (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_leftInverse_of_injective, applied to A₀ viewed as a linear map with LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr). Since ℝᴺ is finite-dimensional, L is continuous (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap), so L ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ) and L ∘L A₀ = id.
2. (Strict derivative of h := L ∘ ψ.) ψ is C¹ at x₀ and the order 1 is nonzero, so ψ is strictly differentiable at x₀ with strict derivative A₀ (ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt; in this Mathlib the side condition is 1 ≠ 0). L is continuous linear, so it is strictly differentiable everywhere with derivative L. By the chain rule (HasStrictFDerivAt.comp), h : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, h(x) := L(ψ(x)), is strictly differentiable at x₀ with derivative L ∘ A₀ = id. This is the identity continuous linear equivalence of ℝⁿ (ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl ℝ (Rn n)).
3. (Inverse function theorem.) ℝⁿ is complete and h has the invertible strict derivative id at x₀. So the local inverse k := HasStrictFDerivAt.localInverse h id x₀ : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ satisfies two properties. (a) k(h(x)) = x for all x in a neighbourhood U of x₀ (HasStrictFDerivAt.eventually_left_inverse). (b) k is strictly differentiable, in particular differentiable, at h(x₀) with derivative id⁻¹ = id (HasStrictFDerivAt.to_localInverse).
4. (Differentiability of g.) Put g := k ∘ L : ℝᴺ → ℝⁿ. L is differentiable at y₀ and L(y₀) = h(x₀), where k is differentiable by 3(b). By the chain rule, g is differentiable at y₀ = ψ(x₀).
5. (Left inverse.) For x ∈ U, g(ψ(x)) = k(L(ψ(x))) = k(h(x)) = x by 3(a). So g(ψ(x)) = x for every x in the neighbourhood U of x₀. Together with step 4 this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose a continuous linear left inverse L of the injective Dψ(x₀) (finite dimension).
L ∘ ψ is strictly differentiable at x₀ with derivative L ∘ Dψ(x₀) = id.
Inverse function theorem: a local inverse k with k(L(ψ x)) = x near x₀, and k differentiable at L(ψ x₀).
g := k ∘ L is differentiable at ψ(x₀) and satisfies g(ψ x) = x near x₀.

subproblems.title: Local differentiable extension of the tangent projection near a C² chart point
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ (ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ satisfy Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M V W ψ. That is: V and W are open, ψ is C² on V, ψ is injective on V, and ψ(V) = W ∩ M. Moreover V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x is injective for every x ∈ V. Assume (T): tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) (= LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) for every x ∈ V. Then for every x₀ ∈ V there is Q : ℝᴺ → L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) with three properties. (i) Q is Fréchet differentiable at ψ(x₀). (ii) tangentProjection M z = Q(z) for every z ∈ M in some neighbourhood of ψ(x₀), i.e. tangentProjection M =ᶠ[𝓝[M] ψ x₀] Q. (iii) Q(ψ(x)) = (range Dψ(x)).starProjection, the orthogonal projection of ℝᴺ onto range Dψ(x), for every x in some neighbourhood of x₀. Here tangentProjection M z := (tangentSpace M z).starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space of the frozen contract.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M V W ψ → (∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) → ∀ x₀ ∈ V, ∃ Q : Rn N → (Rn N →L[ℝ] Rn N), DifferentiableAt ℝ Q (ψ x₀) ∧ tangentProjection M =ᶠ[𝓝[M] ψ x₀] Q ∧ ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, Q (ψ x) = (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap).starProjection
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 of the supplied proof of second_fundamental_form_chart_formula. These are the identification P_{ψ(x)} = Π(Dψ(x)) via (TH1), the left inverse, the localisation in M (Simon 4.2), and the extension P̃ = Π ∘ Dψ ∘ π of the tangent projection near y₀. Hypothesis (T) is the instance of (TH1) for the present chart, which is all those steps use. This proof uses the sibling results range_projection_diff (Submission.sff_range_starProjection_differentiableAt) and immersion_left_inverse (Submission.sff_immersion_local_left_inverse).
Notation: ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d); L(X, Y) := (X →L[ℝ] Y) with the operator norm; for a linear map B, range B := LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap and K.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of the ambient space onto the subspace K. A(x) := Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x. Πr(B) := (LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap).starProjection for B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ). P_z := tangentProjection M z = (tangentSpace M z).starProjection. Fix x₀ ∈ V and put y₀ := ψ(x₀).
1. (Regularity at x₀.) V is open and x₀ ∈ V, so V ∈ 𝓝 x₀. ψ is C² on V, so ContDiffAt ℝ 2 ψ x₀ (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). Hence ψ is C¹ at x₀ (ContDiffAt.of_le), and A = fderiv ℝ ψ is C¹ at x₀ (ContDiffAt.fderiv_right with m = 1, since 1 + 1 ≤ 2). In particular A is differentiable at x₀ (order 1 ≠ 0). A(x₀) is injective by the chart property.
2. (Left inverse; sibling immersion_left_inverse.) Apply immersion_left_inverse to ψ and x₀; its hypotheses ContDiffAt ℝ 1 ψ x₀ and injectivity of A(x₀) hold by step 1. This gives g : ℝᴺ → ℝⁿ, differentiable at y₀, with g(ψ(x)) = x for all x near x₀. Choose an open set U with x₀ ∈ U and g(ψ(x)) = x for all x ∈ U (eventually_nhds_iff; write _root_.eventually_nhds_iff in the contract scope, because Metric is open). In particular g(y₀) = x₀.
3. (Localisation in M; Simon 4.2.) V₀ := U ∩ V is open with x₀ ∈ V₀ ⊆ V. By SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.SubmanifoldTopology; it uses the relative properness of ψ), there is an open W₀ ⊆ W with ψ(V₀) = W₀ ∩ M. Since y₀ = ψ(x₀) ∈ ψ(V₀) = W₀ ∩ M, we get y₀ ∈ W₀, so W₀ ∈ 𝓝 y₀.
4. (Definition of Q; property (i).) Define Q(z) := Πr(A(g(z))) for z ∈ ℝᴺ, i.e. Q = Πr ∘ A ∘ g. g is differentiable at y₀ and g(y₀) = x₀. A is differentiable at x₀ = g(y₀) (step 1). Πr is differentiable at A(x₀) = A(g(y₀)) by the sibling range_projection_diff, because A(x₀) is injective. By the chain rule (DifferentiableAt.comp, after rewriting g(y₀) = x₀), Q is differentiable at y₀.
5. (Property (ii).) Let z ∈ W₀ ∩ M. Then z ∈ ψ(V₀), so z = ψ(x) for some x ∈ V₀ = U ∩ V. Since x ∈ U, g(z) = g(ψ(x)) = x. Hence Q(z) = Πr(A(x)) = (range A(x)).starProjection = (tangentSpace M (ψ x)).starProjection = P_{ψ(x)} = P_z. The third equality uses (T) at x ∈ V: equal subspaces have equal orthogonal projections. [Lean: rewriting the submodule inside .starProjection gives an instance-dependent motive. Use the auxiliary fact ∀ K K' : Submodule ℝ (Rn N), K = K' → K.starProjection = K'.starProjection, proved by `rintro K K' rfl; rfl`; this is valid because HasOrthogonalProjection is a Prop-valued class.] Since W₀ ∈ 𝓝 y₀, P_z = Q(z) for every z ∈ M in a neighbourhood of y₀, i.e. tangentProjection M =ᶠ[𝓝[M] y₀] Q (eventually_nhdsWithin_iff).
6. (Property (iii).) U is an open neighbourhood of x₀, and for x ∈ U we have Q(ψ(x)) = Πr(A(g(ψ(x)))) = Πr(A(x)) = (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap).starProjection. Hence this holds for all x in a neighbourhood of x₀. Steps 4, 5 and 6 give (i), (ii) and (iii) for Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: ψ is C² at x₀, so ψ is C¹ at x₀ and Dψ is differentiable at x₀; Dψ(x₀) is injective.
immersion_left_inverse: g differentiable at ψ(x₀) with g(ψ x) = x on an open U ∋ x₀.
SimonGMT exists_open_image_eq_inter: an open W₀ with ψ(U ∩ V) = W₀ ∩ M, and ψ(x₀) ∈ W₀.
Q := Πr ∘ Dψ ∘ g is differentiable at ψ(x₀) by range_projection_diff and the chain rule.
On W₀ ∩ M, z = ψ(x) with g(z) = x, so Q(z) = Πr(Dψ x) = tangentProjection M z by (T).
For x ∈ U, Q(ψ x) = Πr(Dψ x).

subproblems.title: Derivative of an operator field that fixes the chart tangent vectors (B = (D²ψ)^⊥ computation)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ (ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ, Q : ℝᴺ → L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) and x₀ ∈ ℝⁿ. Assume four things: ψ is differentiable at x₀; the derivative map x ↦ Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x, from ℝⁿ to L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), is differentiable at x₀; Q is differentiable at ψ(x₀); and Q(ψ(x))(Dψ(x)v) = Dψ(x)v for all v ∈ ℝⁿ and all x in some neighbourhood of x₀. Then for all a, b ∈ ℝⁿ: DQ(ψ(x₀))(Dψ(x₀)a)(Dψ(x₀)b) = D²ψ(x₀)[a, b] − Q(ψ(x₀))(D²ψ(x₀)[a, b]). Here DQ(y) = fderiv ℝ Q y ∈ L(ℝᴺ, L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ)) and D²ψ(x₀)[a, b] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ a b.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (Q : Rn N → (Rn N →L[ℝ] Rn N)) (x₀ : Rn n), DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ x₀ → DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ → DifferentiableAt ℝ Q (ψ x₀) → (∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, ∀ v : Rn n, Q (ψ x) (fderiv ℝ ψ x v) = fderiv ℝ ψ x v) → ∀ a b : Rn n, fderiv ℝ Q (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ a) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ b) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ a b - Q (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ a b)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 (parent G2, the computation of L₀) of the supplied proof of second_fundamental_form_chart_formula. That step differentiates the identity P̃(ψ(x))(Dψ(x)b) = Dψ(x)b at x₀ in direction a. Here the operator field is an arbitrary Q with the fixing property.
Notation: y₀ := ψ(x₀); A(x) := Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x; A₀ := A(x₀); L₀ := DQ(y₀) = fderiv ℝ Q y₀ ∈ L(ℝᴺ, L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ)); D := DA(x₀) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ ∈ L(ℝⁿ, L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ)), so that D²ψ(x₀)[a, b] = D a b. Fix a, b ∈ ℝⁿ.
1. (Chain rule.) ψ has derivative A₀ at x₀ and Q has derivative L₀ at y₀. So c(x) := Q(ψ(x)) ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) has derivative L₀ ∘ A₀ at x₀ (HasFDerivAt.comp).
2. (Derivative of x ↦ A(x)b.) u(x) := A(x)b applies the operator-valued map A, which has derivative D at x₀, to the constant vector b, which has derivative 0. By the product rule for applying an operator-valued map to a vector-valued map (HasFDerivAt.clm_apply), u has derivative u′ := A₀ ∘ 0 + D.flip b at x₀. That is, u′(a′) = D a′ b for a′ ∈ ℝⁿ.
3. (Product rule for G.) Let G(x) := c(x)(u(x)) = Q(ψ(x))(A(x)b). By HasFDerivAt.clm_apply applied to steps 1 and 2, G has derivative G′ := c(x₀) ∘ u′ + (L₀ ∘ A₀).flip (u(x₀)) at x₀. That is, G′(a′) = Q(y₀)(D a′ b) + L₀(A₀a′)(A₀b).
4. (G = u near x₀.) By hypothesis with v := b, G(x) = Q(ψ(x))(A(x)b) = A(x)b = u(x) for all x in a neighbourhood of x₀. So u′ is also a derivative of G at x₀ (HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). By uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative (HasFDerivAt.unique), G′ = u′. Evaluating at a′ = a gives Q(y₀)(D a b) + L₀(A₀a)(A₀b) = D a b.
5. (Rearranging.) L₀(A₀a)(A₀b) = D a b − Q(y₀)(D a b), i.e. fderiv ℝ Q (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ a) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ b) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ a b − Q (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x₀ a b). ∎
proof_key_steps: Chain rule: D(Q ∘ ψ)(x₀) = DQ(ψ x₀) ∘ Dψ(x₀).
D(x ↦ Dψ(x)b)(x₀)a = D²ψ(x₀)[a, b] (clm_apply with a constant vector).
Product rule (clm_apply) for x ↦ Q(ψ x)(Dψ(x)b).
This map equals x ↦ Dψ(x)b near x₀, and Fréchet derivatives are unique.
Evaluate at a and rearrange.

subproblems.title: Derivative within M along chart directions equals the derivative of a local extension
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ (ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ, f, g : ℝᴺ → L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) and x₀ ∈ ℝⁿ. Assume five things: V is a neighbourhood of x₀; ψ(V) ⊆ M; ψ is differentiable at x₀; g is differentiable at ψ(x₀); and f(z) = g(z) for every z ∈ M in some neighbourhood of ψ(x₀), i.e. f =ᶠ[𝓝[M] ψ x₀] g. Then for every a ∈ ℝⁿ, fderivWithin ℝ f M (ψ x₀) (Dψ(x₀)a) = Dg(ψ(x₀))(Dψ(x₀)a) in L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ). Here Dψ(x₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ and Dg(y) = fderiv ℝ g y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (f g : Rn N → (Rn N →L[ℝ] Rn N)) (x₀ : Rn n), V ∈ 𝓝 x₀ → ψ '' V ⊆ M → DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ x₀ → DifferentiableAt ℝ g (ψ x₀) → f =ᶠ[𝓝[M] ψ x₀] g → ∀ a : Rn n, fderivWithin ℝ f M (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ a) = fderiv ℝ g (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ a)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6–7 of the supplied proof of second_fundamental_form_chart_formula, i.e. the derivative of P within M and the fact that chart directions lie in the tangent cone. M need not have unique differentiability at ψ(x₀), so fderivWithin is only determined on the tangent cone; this lemma evaluates it on chart directions only.
Notation: y₀ := ψ(x₀), A₀ := Dψ(x₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀, L₀ := Dg(y₀) = fderiv ℝ g y₀. Fix a ∈ ℝⁿ.
1. (y₀ ∈ M and f(y₀) = g(y₀).) V ∈ 𝓝 x₀ implies x₀ ∈ V (mem_of_mem_nhds), so y₀ = ψ(x₀) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ M. An eventual equality in 𝓝[M] y₀ holds at y₀ when y₀ ∈ M (Filter.EventuallyEq.eq_of_nhdsWithin), so f(y₀) = g(y₀).
2. (L₀ is a derivative of f within M.) g has Fréchet derivative L₀ at y₀, hence also derivative L₀ within M at y₀ (HasFDerivAt.hasFDerivWithinAt). f = g on M near y₀ and f(y₀) = g(y₀) by step 1. So HasFDerivWithinAt f L₀ M y₀ (HasFDerivWithinAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
3. (fderivWithin is a derivative within M.) By step 2, f is differentiable within M at y₀. So HasFDerivWithinAt f (fderivWithin ℝ f M y₀) M y₀ (DifferentiableWithinAt.hasFDerivWithinAt). This holds in all cases, including when y₀ is isolated in M.
4. (Uniqueness on the tangent cone.) Two derivatives of f within M at y₀ agree on tangentConeAt ℝ M y₀ (HasFDerivWithinAt.unique_on). So fderivWithin ℝ f M y₀ v = L₀ v for every v ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ M y₀.
5. (A₀a is in the tangent cone.) ψ has derivative A₀ at x₀, hence also within V at x₀. Since V ∈ 𝓝 x₀, tangentConeAt ℝ V x₀ = ℝⁿ (tangentConeAt_of_mem_nhds), so a ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ V x₀. By HasFDerivWithinAt.mapsTo_tangent_cone, A₀a ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ (ψ '' V) y₀. Since ψ '' V ⊆ M, tangentConeAt_mono gives A₀a ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ M y₀. [Directly: with c_k := k and d_k := ψ(x₀ + a/k) − y₀, we have y₀ + d_k ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ M for large k, d_k → 0 and c_k d_k → A₀a.]
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 5 with v := A₀a: fderivWithin ℝ f M (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ a) = fderiv ℝ g (ψ x₀) (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ a). ∎
proof_key_steps: ψ(x₀) ∈ M, hence f(ψ x₀) = g(ψ x₀).
HasFDerivWithinAt f (Dg(ψ x₀)) M (ψ x₀), by congruence with g.
fderivWithin ℝ f M (ψ x₀) is also a derivative of f within M.
Derivatives within M agree on the tangent cone (unique_on).
Dψ(x₀)a lies in the tangent cone of M at ψ(x₀) (mapsTo_tangent_cone, tangentConeAt_of_mem_nhds, tangentConeAt_mono).
